plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $5 ensures I only win when profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and maximizes expected profit. I'll bid my true value.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks winning at a price above your value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, the theoretically optimal and risk-free approach is to bid exactly my private value of $44.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding your true value maximizes your expected profit - bidding higher risks overpaying, bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value of $29, I should bid $29 to maximize expected long-run profit.
